# Meic Llewellyn

> Meic Llewellyn is a writer from Aberteifi (Cardigan) who lives in Bro Ddyfi, west Wales. His stories celebrate the culture of rural Wales: its music, poetry and the Welsh language. He is the author of *Beware your Dreams…*, a trilogy of stories in one book (paperback, ISBN 978-1-918101-02-7, RRP £8.50), and is writing *Stallion Girl* (working title), a standalone story set in west Wales in 1918.

Official website: https://meicllewellyn.co.uk/
Contact for publishers, agents, press, bookshops and events: meic.tycerrig@gmail.com

## Books

### Beware your Dreams…
- Format: paperback. ISBN 978-1-918101-02-7. RRP £8.50.
- Printed by Y Lolfa, Talybont. Cover image © Therese Urbanska. Illustration by Nigel Gerke.
- A very contemporary trilogy linking the visible world and the unseen, rooted in myth and the reality of life on a small mountain farm in west Wales. Join Gwinnie as she seeks to understand why she can suddenly fly, where her uncle disappears to at night, and where she really belongs. Learn with her how to deliver lambs, how to talk to panthers, where Welsh fairies sleep, and when to turn yourself into a mouse. Share her coming-of-age journey, underground, overground and in deep water, before joining her in a struggle against dark and dangerous, all-too-human, adversaries.
- Weaves Cymraeg (the Welsh language) into the story.

### Stallion Girl (working title, forthcoming)
- A standalone story, not part of the trilogy. Set in west Wales in 1918.
- Not all the wandering stallion men were Roma, but many of them were. Not all the musicians and instrument makers were Roma, but most of them were. And not all the best horse-breeders, developing and perfecting the Welsh Cob, were Roma, but a good few were. The Roma made up a vivid, elusive thread in the culture of this war-weary, impoverished and divided nation, and this story tells of a Roma teenager finding her own way, and finding herself in the process, at a time of intense crisis and desperate decisions.

## About Meic
Meic Llewellyn grew up in Aberteifi (Cardigan), west Wales, until moving with his family to London as a teenager. After university he returned to Wales to help his auntie on a farm in north Pembrokeshire before becoming a teacher. He taught History, English and Media in Wales, Scotland and England, then studied for a PhD at Aberystwyth University. Since then he has been organising and co-ordinating cultural projects drawing together communities in the smaller languages of Europe. He has written poetry and told stories all his life, in both English and Welsh; *Beware your Dreams…* is his first full-length book, written to celebrate the culture, wildlife and landscape of west Wales. He lives on a smallholding in Bro Ddyfi with his wife Angela, and is working on a second book about the Roma 'stallion men' who moved from farm to farm in Ceredigion over a hundred years ago.

## In Meic's words
"It's music, poetry and the Welsh language, all bound up together and an integral part of our way of life. The culture belongs to everyone; we don't have special 'cultured classes' or 'cultured people'. Your bus driver today might be a fiddler or harpist, the farmer over there is quite possibly a bard, those teenagers on the corner could be dancing clogsian (clog dancing) this evening in the village hall, or singing in a choir. The culture is our common possession, the air we breathe. We're predominately a Celtic people, and like all Celts feel close to the animal kingdom and the world of the spirit. Our farm animals are our families, the wild creatures our friends and confidants. And the otherworld is never very far away. That's what I try to celebrate."

## Themes
The Roma in Wales and Roma decoration; the Welsh Cob; Strata Florida Abbey; the family farmhouse as a hub of the community; clog dancing (clogsian) and the National Eisteddfod; the triple harp, Wales' national instrument; red kites over Ceredigion; the Afanc of Welsh legend; music in the tavern; orphan lambs; the Welsh language.

## Frequently asked questions

### Who is Meic Llewellyn?
Meic Llewellyn is a writer who grew up in Aberteifi (Cardigan) and lives on a smallholding in Bro Ddyfi. A former teacher with a PhD from Aberystwyth University, he has written poetry and told stories all his life, in English and Welsh. He writes to celebrate the culture of rural Wales: its music, poetry and the Welsh language, which belong to everyone.

### What is Beware your Dreams… about?
Beware your Dreams… is a trilogy of stories in one book, linking the visible world and the unseen, rooted in myth and life on a small mountain farm in west Wales. It follows Gwinnie as she discovers she can fly, learns where her uncle disappears to at night, and searches for where she really belongs.

### What is Stallion Girl?
Stallion Girl (working title) is Meic’s next book, a standalone story set in west Wales in 1918. It tells of a Roma teenager finding her own way, and finding herself, at a time of intense crisis and desperate decisions.

### How can I get a copy of Beware your Dreams…?
It is available in paperback (ISBN 978-1-918101-02-7, RRP £8.50). Ask your local bookshop, quoting the ISBN, or email Meic at meic.tycerrig@gmail.com.

### Can Meic visit our bookshop, library or festival?
Bookshops, libraries and festivals are warmly invited to get in touch about hosting a reading or signing. Email meic.tycerrig@gmail.com.

### How do publishers, agents and press get in touch?
Email meic.tycerrig@gmail.com for review copies, sample chapters, the press kit, interviews and rights enquiries.
